open_questions.text: The component values of Item.Properties#pickaxe/axe/shovel/hoe/sword/spear/humanoidArmor are modelled from the vanilla 26.3 items in Pumpkin's assets/items.json (an extractor dump), not from decompiled source. `generate_manifest.dart --verify-vanilla` re-checks the model against every vanilla tool, spear and armor piece of the tiers it knows.

The sword, dagger and war axe classes override hurtEnemy with hurtAndBreak(1). If vanilla 26.3 also applies the Weapon component's item_damage_per_attack (1) after a hit, those items lose 2 durability per hit. Not verified against the decompiled game.
Whether Items.NETHERITE_*.isCorrectToolForDrops(omnitoolStack, state) uses the passed stack's Tool component (then the override equals the pickaxe rules) or the netherite item's own is not verified.
Spears of non-wooden materials get the default spear sounds (item.spear.*); only the wooden tier differs in vanilla.

Block properties the mod does not set (friction, speed/jump factor, map colour, instrument, push reaction) are the BlockBehaviour.Properties.of() defaults and are not parsed; vanilla_defaults lists the ones that were assumed.
None of the mod's items call fireResistant(), so unlike netherite gear they carry no minecraft:damage_resistant component and burn in lava.

Items and the block are listed in registration order; with NeoForge's DeferredRegister that order decides the numeric ids after the vanilla ones. The id mapping actually used must come from the registry sync, not from here.

behaviors.summary: Two grey tooltip lines on the wardframe item. Client only.
The class extends vanilla MaceItem, which gives it the smash attack (fall distance above 1.5, bonus damage, knockback and sounds). It overrides nothing itself.

Mining speed is the material speed on any block in the pickaxe, axe, shovel or hoe mineable tags or #minecraft:sword_efficient, else 1.0. The Tool component alone (pickaxe rules) gives it only on pickaxe blocks.

ORs Items.NETHERITE_{PICKAXE,AXE,SHOVEL,HOE,SWORD}.isCorrectToolForDrops(stack, state). The stack passed is the omnitool's own, and the vanilla implementation reads the stack's Tool component, so this is believed to equal the omnitool's own Tool rules (the pickaxe rules). Unverified.
Right click on a block: tries the vanilla axe, then (hoe, shovel; swapped while sneaking) block transformers on the held stack, and damages it like the dedicated tools.

Pickaxe classes: after a block with non-zero hardness is mined on the server, hurtAndBreak(1). The Tool component's damage_per_block already does this (1 by default) in vanilla's Item.mineBlock, so the override is believed redundant.
Per entity: empty shape for players, tamed TamableAnimals and any entity with a player passenger; a full cube for everything else and for queries without an entity (pathfinding).
Never pathfindable: mobs treat every wardframe as a wall.
A placed wardframe sets each of its six face properties to whether that neighbour is a wardframe.
Six boolean properties north, south, east, west, up, down.
When a neighbour changes, the face property of that direction is recomputed (true when the neighbour is a wardframe).

Sword, dagger and war axe classes: hurtAndBreak(1) when an enemy is hurt. Vanilla also charges the Weapon component's item_damage_per_attack (1) per attack, so these items may lose 2 durability per hit. Unverified.

Only players and their pets may pass.
Adjacent frames merge into a single doorway.
